Story · Lesson 1

It Won't Rain!

Omar is sure about the weather for the picnic. Read the story, then read Omar's side of it.

Say what you think will happenMake a promiseOffer to do something

1The story

It is August, the rainy season. Adam, Sara, and Omar are planning a picnic by the Nile on Friday. Sara looks at the sky. "I think it will rain on Friday," she says.

Omar shows them his phone. "Look at my weather app. It won't rain. Friday will be sunny and hot. I promise!" Adam isn't sure. "Will we need umbrellas?" "No, you won't," Omar says. "Trust me. It will be a perfect day."

On Friday, the friends meet by the river. Sara brings sandwiches, Adam brings juice, and Omar brings a big bag of fruit. The sky is blue, and the sun is hot. "You see?" Omar says. "I told you!"

Then, at four o'clock, the sky turns dark. A strong wind comes, and big drops of rain start to fall. In two minutes, everybody is wet. Sara laughs. "Your app was wrong, Omar!" Omar looks at his phone. "Oh no. My app shows the weather in London!" "Don't worry," Adam says. "Next time, I'll check the weather. And I'll bring umbrellas!"

2Questions and answers Answer fast. Short answers are fine.

1
What season is it?The rainy season.
2
What are the friends planning?A picnic by the Nile.
3
What does Sara think?She thinks it will rain.
4
Does Omar think it will rain?No, he doesn't. He says it won't rain.
5
What does Omar promise?Friday will be sunny and hot.
6
Will they need umbrellas, says Omar?No, they won't.
7
What does Sara bring?Sandwiches.
8
Who brings fruit?Omar.
9
What happens at four o'clock?The sky turns dark, and it starts to rain.
10
Why was Omar's app wrong?It showed the weather in London!
11
Who will check the weather next time?Adam.
12
What will Adam bring next time?Umbrellas.

3Point of view Now Omar tells his side of the story.

O

It's August, the rainy season, and my friends and I are planning a picnic by the Nile. Sara thinks it will rain. But look at my weather app! It won't rain. Friday will be sunny and hot. I promise!

"Will we need umbrellas?" Adam asks. "No, you won't. Trust me. It will be a perfect day."

On Friday, the sky is blue, and the sun is hot. "You see?" I say. Then, at four o'clock, the sky turns dark, and the rain comes. Everybody is wet!

I look at my phone. Oh no. My app shows the weather in London! Next time, I'll check the city first. And I'll listen to Sara!

4What did you learn?

You learned will and won't.

We use them to say what we think about the future, to promise, and to decide or offer something at the moment we speak.

We use will to…Example
say what we think will happenI think it will rain on Friday.
promiseIt will be a perfect day. I promise!
decide now, or offer helpNext time, I'll bring umbrellas!
say no, or askIt won't rain. · Will we need umbrellas?
will + verb, the same for everyoneI will, she will, they will.
Short forms: 'll · won'tI'll = I will. won't = will not.
going to or will?A plan: I'm going to travel. A quick decision: I'll help you!
QuestionsWill it rain tomorrow?Yes, it will. / No, it won't.

5New words

picnica meal outside, in a park or by a river
appa program on a phone
promisesay that you will really do something
trustbelieve that someone is right or honest
dropssmall round pieces of water
wetcovered with water

Topic · Lesson 2

Tomorrow's Weather

How to understand a weather forecast, and what to do with it.

Understand a weather forecastSay what the weather will be likePlan your day

1Read

Every evening, the TV news and many phone apps give the weather forecast. The forecast tells us what the weather will be like tomorrow and in the next few days.

Here is the forecast for tomorrow. In Khartoum, it will be sunny and very hot, with a high of forty-two degrees. In Port Sudan, it will be hot and humid, but there won't be any rain. In Kassala, there will be clouds in the morning, and there will be storms in the afternoon.

The temperature at night will be lower, about twenty-eight degrees in Khartoum. Forecasts are not always right, but they help us plan our day. When the forecast says "rain," take an umbrella. When it says "very hot," drink a lot of water and stay out of the sun at noon.

2Tomorrow

Khartoumsunny · high of 42°
Port Sudanhot and humid · no rain
Kassalaclouds, then storms

3Questions and answers Answer fast. Short answers are fine.

1
What does the weather forecast tell us?What the weather will be like tomorrow and in the next few days.
2
What will the weather be like in Khartoum tomorrow?Sunny and very hot.
3
What will the high be in Khartoum?Forty-two degrees.
4
Will there be any rain in Port Sudan?No, there won't.
5
When will there be storms in Kassala?In the afternoon.
6
What do you take when the forecast says rain?An umbrella.

4New words

forecastwhat experts think the weather will be
fewa small number
highthe hottest temperature of the day
temperaturehow hot or cold something is
plandecide what you will do
noontwelve o'clock in the middle of the day

I'll Call You Back

Calling a friend's home and leaving a message

Ask for someone on the phoneLeave a messageOffer and promise to help

1Read the conversation

Sara calls Adam's home. His mother answers the phone.
MHMRS. HASSANHello?
SSARAHello, Mrs. Hassan. It's Sara, Adam's friend. Can I speak to Adam, please?
MHMRS. HASSANHi, Sara. I'm sorry, he isn't here. He's at the market.
SSARAOh. Can I leave a message?
MHMRS. HASSANOf course. I'll write it down.
SSARAPlease tell him the test is on Sunday, not Monday.
MHMRS. HASSANSunday, not Monday. OK, I'll tell him when he comes home.
SSARAThank you. And can he call me back tonight?
MHMRS. HASSANSure. I'll ask him to call you back.
SSARAThanks a lot. Goodbye!

2Useful phrases

Ask for someone

Can I speak to Adam, please?
— I'm sorry, he isn't here.

Leave a message

Can I leave a message?
— Of course.

Give the message

Please tell him the test is on Sunday.

Offer

I'll write it down.

Promise

I'll tell him when he comes home.

Ask for a call

Can he call me back?
— Sure.

3New words

leave a messagegive information for someone who isn't there
write it downwrite it on paper so you don't forget
call you backcall you again later

Story · Lesson 4

Omar's New Job

Omar works at a phone repair shop now, and there are rules. Read the story, then read it from Omar's point of view.

Talk about rulesSay what is not necessaryGive advice

1The story

Omar has a new part-time job. He works at a phone repair shop near the market, three evenings a week. On his first day, the owner, Mr. Kamal, explains the rules.

"You have to be here at five o'clock, and you have to stay until nine. You don't have to wear a suit. A clean shirt is fine. And you don't have to work on Fridays." Omar smiles. Friday is football day!

"You should be polite to every customer, even when they are angry. And you shouldn't use your phone when you are working. Customers have to wait, so you should work quickly, but carefully."

On Omar's first evening, a woman comes in with a broken screen. She is in a hurry. "Can you fix it today? I have to call my son tonight!" Omar works quickly but carefully, and in forty minutes, the phone works. The woman is very happy. "He should get a raise!" she tells Mr. Kamal. Mr. Kamal laughs. "He has to work here for more than one day first!"

2Questions and answers Answer fast. Short answers are fine.

1
Where does Omar work?At a phone repair shop near the market.
2
How many evenings a week does he work?Three.
3
What time does he have to be at the shop?At five o'clock.
4
Does he have to wear a suit?No, he doesn't. A clean shirt is fine.
5
Does he have to work on Fridays?No, he doesn't.
6
Why is Omar happy about that?Friday is football day!
7
How should he be with customers?Polite, even when they are angry.
8
Should he use his phone at work?No, he shouldn't.
9
What is wrong with the woman's phone?It has a broken screen.
10
Why is she in a hurry?She has to call her son tonight.
11
How long does Omar need?Forty minutes.
12
What does Mr. Kamal say about a raise?Omar has to work there for more than one day first!

3Point of view Now Omar tells his story.

O

I have a new part-time job! I work at a phone repair shop near the market, three evenings a week. On my first day, the owner, Mr. Kamal, explained the rules.

I have to be at the shop at five o'clock, and I have to stay until nine. I don't have to wear a suit, and I don't have to work on Fridays. Great! Friday is football day.

I should be polite to every customer, even angry ones, and I shouldn't use my phone at work. Customers have to wait, so I should work quickly, but carefully.

On my first evening, a woman came in with a broken screen. She had to call her son that night, and I fixed it in forty minutes! "He should get a raise!" she said. Mr. Kamal laughed. "He has to work here for more than one day first!"

4What did you learn?

You learned have to and should.

have to: it is a rule, it is necessary. should: it is a good idea, it is advice.

A rule: necessaryAdvice: a good idea
I have to be here at five.You should be polite.
He has to stay until nine.He should work carefully.
You don't have to wear a suit.You shouldn't use your phone.
Do I have to work on Friday?Should I call him?
he · she · it → has toOmar has to be there at five.
don't have to = not necessaryYou don't have to wear a suit. You can if you want.
should + verb, the same for everyoneI should, she should, they should.
QuestionsDo you have to work on Fridays?No, I don't. Friday is my day off.

5New words

part-timefor only some hours of the week
repairfixing something that is broken
ownerthe person a shop or a thing belongs to
politespeaking and acting in a kind and correct way
in a hurryneeding to do something fast
raisemore money for your work

Topic · Lesson 5

Healthy Habits

Sleep, water, food and moving your body, and what doctors say we should do.

Talk about healthy habitsGive adviceSay what is necessary and what is not

1Read

Good habits keep us healthy. Doctors say we should sleep seven or eight hours every night. Many students sleep less, and they feel tired in class.

In a hot country like Sudan, we should drink a lot of water, about two liters a day, or more in summer. We shouldn't wait until we are thirsty.

We should eat fruit and vegetables every day, and we shouldn't eat too much sugar. Sweet tea is delicious, but four cups a day with a lot of sugar is not good for us.

We also have to move our bodies. You don't have to go to a gym. You can walk to the shop, play football with friends, or take the stairs. Thirty minutes a day is enough. And one more habit, put your phone down an hour before bed. Your eyes and your brain will thank you!

2Every day

sleep7 to 8 hours
waterabout 2 liters
fruit and vegetablesevery day
move30 minutes

3Questions and answers Answer fast. Short answers are fine.

1
How many hours should we sleep?Seven or eight hours.
2
How much water should we drink?About two liters a day, or more in summer.
3
Should we wait until we are thirsty?No, we shouldn't.
4
Is a lot of sweet tea good for us?No, it isn't.
5
Do we have to go to a gym?No, we don't. We can walk or play football.
6
When should we put the phone down?An hour before bed.

4New words

habitsthings you do again and again
healthywell; not sick
thirstyneeding to drink
delicioustasting very good
gyma place with machines for exercise
brainthe part of your head that thinks

How Do I Get to the Bank?

Asking for and giving directions in the street

Ask the wayUnderstand directionsThank someone for help

1Read the conversation

Omar needs to send money to his family in Port Sudan. He is looking for the bank near the hospital.
OOMARExcuse me. How do I get to the bank?
SKSHOPKEEPERWhich bank? There are two.
OOMARThe big one, near the hospital.
SKSHOPKEEPEROh, that's not far. Go straight down this street.
OOMARStraight down this street. OK.
SKSHOPKEEPERThen turn left at the traffic lights. You have to cross the bridge.
OOMARTurn left, then cross the bridge. Can I walk there?
SKSHOPKEEPERYes, it's fifteen minutes on foot. But it's very hot, so you should take a rickshaw.
OOMARThank you very much!
SKSHOPKEEPERYou're welcome. The bank is on the right, next to the hospital.

2Useful phrases

Ask the way

How do I get to the bank?

Go straight

Go straight down this street.

Turn

Turn left at the traffic lights.

Cross

You have to cross the bridge.

Give advice

You should take a rickshaw.

Say where it is

It's on the right, next to the hospital.

3New words

Story · Lesson 7

Adam Has Never Flown

Adam wants to be a pilot, but he has never been on a plane. Read the story, then read Adam's story after his first flight.

Talk about life experiencesAsk: Have you ever…?Say when something happened

1The story

Adam wants to be a pilot. He has read a lot of books about planes, and he has watched hundreds of videos. He knows the names of all the big airports in the world. But there is one problem. Adam has never been on a plane!

His friends ask him questions. "Have you ever flown?" "No, I haven't." "Have you ever been to an airport?" "Yes, I have. I have seen the planes from the window." Omar laughs. "A pilot who has never flown!"

Then one day, Adam's uncle calls from Port Sudan. "Adam, I have bought you a ticket. You are going to fly to Port Sudan next week!" Adam can't believe it.

Now Adam is at the airport. He has checked in, and he has found his seat by the window. The plane is moving. Adam is excited and a little nervous. He looks out of the window and smiles. "Finally," he says. "I'm flying!"

2Questions and answers Answer fast. Short answers are fine.

1
What does Adam want to be?A pilot.
2
Has he read a lot of books about planes?Yes, he has.
3
Has he watched videos about planes?Yes, he has. Hundreds!
4
Has Adam ever been on a plane?No, he hasn't.
5
Has he ever been to an airport?Yes, he has.
6
What has he seen from the window?The planes.
7
Who laughs at him?Omar.
8
Who calls Adam?His uncle, from Port Sudan.
9
What has his uncle bought?A ticket for Adam.
10
Where is Adam going to fly?To Port Sudan.
11
Has Adam found his seat?Yes, he has. It's by the window.
12
How does Adam feel?Excited, and a little nervous.

3Point of view Now it is after the flight. Adam tells when everything happened.

A

I always wanted to be a pilot. When I was a child, I read books about planes, and last year I watched hundreds of videos. But I wasn't on a plane, not once.

Last month, my uncle called from Port Sudan. "I bought you a ticket!" he said. I couldn't believe it.

Last Tuesday, I went to the airport. I checked in and found my seat by the window. When the plane took off, I looked out of the window and smiled.

Now I can say it: I have flown! And one day, I'm going to fly the plane myself.

4What did you learn?

You learned the present perfect.

We use it for experiences in our life until now, when we don't say when. When we say when, we use the past simple.

Present perfect: we don't say whenPast simple: we say when
I have seen the planes.I saw the planes yesterday.
His uncle has bought a ticket.His uncle bought it last month.
Sara has never been to Kassala.Sara went to Port Sudan in 2020.
Have you ever flown? Yes, I have.When did you fly? Last Tuesday.
have / has + past participleI have seen, he has bought, they have flown.
ever in questions, never for noHave you ever flown? I have never flown.
Some verbs change: been · flown · seenbe → been, fly → flown, see → seen, buy → bought
QuestionsHave you ever been on a plane?Yes, I have. / No, I haven't.

5New words

airportsplaces where planes arrive and leave
ticketa paper or code that lets you travel
believethink that something is true
checked ingave your name and bag at the airport before a flight
seata place to sit
finallyafter a long time

Topic · Lesson 8

The Pyramids of Sudan

Sudan has more pyramids than Egypt. Have you ever seen them?

Talk about a famous placeUse the present perfect for experiencesTalk about history

1Read

When people think of pyramids, they usually think of Egypt. But Sudan has more pyramids than Egypt, more than two hundred!

The most famous ones are at Meroe, about two hundred kilometers north of Khartoum. Meroe was the capital of the Kingdom of Kush more than two thousand years ago. The kings and queens of Kush built their pyramids there.

The pyramids of Meroe are smaller than the pyramids in Egypt, and they are steeper. Many of them have small temples next to them.

Thousands of tourists have visited Meroe, and scientists have studied it for many years. In 2011, it became a World Heritage Site. Have you ever seen the pyramids of Meroe? Many Sudanese people have never visited them. Maybe you will be the first in your family!

2Meroe in numbers

200+pyramids in Sudan
200 kmnorth of Khartoum
2,000+years old
2011a World Heritage Site

3Questions and answers Answer fast. Short answers are fine.

1
Which country has more pyramids, Sudan or Egypt?Sudan. It has more than two hundred.
2
Where are the most famous pyramids in Sudan?At Meroe.
3
How far is Meroe from Khartoum?About two hundred kilometers.
4
Who built the pyramids?The kings and queens of Kush.
5
Are they bigger than the pyramids in Egypt?No, they aren't. They are smaller and steeper.
6
Have many tourists visited Meroe?Yes, they have. Thousands have visited it.

4New words

kingdoma country with a king or a queen
builtthe past of build
steepergoing up more quickly
templesold buildings where people prayed
touristspeople who travel to visit places
scientistspeople who study the world in a careful way

Story · Lesson 10

The Big Test

The last test of the Pre-Intermediate stage is coming, and Omar is worried. Read the story, then read it from Omar's point of view.

Talk about a possible futureUse if and willGive and get help

1The story

The Pre-Intermediate final test is next Sunday. Everybody is studying, but Omar is worried. "If I fail the test, I will have to repeat the level," he says. "And if I repeat the level, I won't be in your class!"

Sara has an idea. "If we study together every evening, we will all pass." Adam agrees. "If you come to my house, my mother will make tea and cake!" So every evening, the three friends study at Adam's house.

They read the old stories again. They ask each other questions, like Mr. Ali in class. "If I ask you a question, you have to answer fast!" Sara says. Omar learns a lot, and he even starts to enjoy it.

On Sunday, Omar sits down in the test room. He reads the first question and smiles. He knows the answer. A week later, Mr. Ali comes into class with the results. "Omar, ninety-one. Sara, ninety-four. Adam, ninety-two. Congratulations! If you keep working like this, you will do great in Intermediate 1!"

2Questions and answers Answer fast. Short answers are fine.

1
When is the final test?Next Sunday.
2
Who is worried?Omar.
3
What will happen if Omar fails?He will have to repeat the level.
4
What is Sara's idea?To study together every evening.
5
What will Adam's mother do if they come?She will make tea and cake.
6
Where do the friends study?At Adam's house.
7
What do they do?They read the old stories again and ask each other questions.
8
Does Omar start to enjoy studying?Yes, he does.
9
Why does Omar smile in the test room?He knows the answer to the first question.
10
What is Omar's result?Ninety-one.
11
Who has the best result?Sara, with ninety-four.
12
What will happen if they keep working like this?They will do great in Intermediate 1.

3Point of view Now Omar tells the story.

O

The final test is next Sunday, and I'm worried. If I fail the test, I'll have to repeat the level. And if I repeat the level, I won't be in my friends' class!

Then Sara has an idea. "If we study together every evening, we'll all pass." And Adam says, "If you come to my house, my mother'll make tea and cake!"

So every evening, we read the old stories again and ask each other questions. I learn a lot, and I even start to enjoy it.

On Sunday, I read the first question and smile. I know the answer! A week later, Mr. Ali has the results, and I have ninety-one. If I keep working like this, I'll do great in Intermediate 1!

4What did you learn?

You learned the first conditional.

We use it to talk about a possible future: if one thing happens, another thing will happen.

If + presentwill + verb
If I fail the test,I will have to repeat the level.
If we study together,we will all pass.
If you come to my house,my mother will make tea.
If it doesn't rain,we won't need umbrellas.
After if: the presentIf I study. Not: if I will study.
Then: will · won't + verbwe will pass, we won't fail
Two orders, the same meaningIf we study, we'll pass. = We'll pass if we study.
QuestionsWhat will you do if you pass?If I pass, I'll go to the next level.

5New words

finalthe last
failnot pass a test
repeatdo again
agreesthinks the same
enjoylike doing something
resultsthe numbers you get in a test

Topic · Lesson 11

How to Study Well

Five ideas from teachers and scientists, and what will happen if you try them.

Give tips for studyingUse if and willTalk about your study habits

1Read

Good students don't only study hard. They study well. Here are some ideas from teachers and scientists.

Study a little every day. If you study for thirty minutes every day, you will remember more than after five hours the night before a test.

Sleep well. Your brain saves new information when you sleep. If you sleep less than six hours, you won't remember your lessons well.

Say it out loud. If you read the stories out loud, you will learn the pronunciation, too. And if you teach a friend, you will understand it better.

Turn off your phone. If your phone is next to you, you will look at it every few minutes. Take breaks. Study for twenty-five minutes, then rest for five. If you do this, your brain will stay fresh.

2Five ideas

30 minutesevery day
sleepmore than six hours
out loudread, and teach a friend
phone offno messages while you study
25 + 5study, then rest

3Questions and answers Answer fast. Short answers are fine.

1
Is it better to study every day or the night before a test?Every day.
2
What does your brain do when you sleep?It saves new information.
3
What will happen if you sleep less than six hours?You won't remember your lessons well.
4
What will you learn if you read out loud?The pronunciation.
5
What will happen if your phone is next to you?You will look at it every few minutes.
6
How long should you study before a break?Twenty-five minutes.

4New words
